Store $FF in the actor slot's field at $EA50,X and return.

Initialize the actor's size and extent fields and clear the shared sequence flags at $1D/$1F. Set the linked-actor state through $C47F and allocate types $28, $29 and $2A with their parent fields pointing back to this slot.
For the actor slot in X, set state $04 at $E930,X, set $EA50,X to $FF and set bit 4 at $E810,X. The initializer at $C435 calls this before allocating the three linked slots.
Set the slot extent fields and bit 7 of $EB10. Fall through to the common initializer at $C4AC.
Store state five, set bit 2 in the slot flags and initialize $E870,X to $0F.
Set both slot size fields to two and $EA50,X to $FF.
Set width and height fields to nine and sixteen, set $E9F0/$EA80 to three and five, then set motion and timing fields before entering $C4AC.
Set flag bit 4, place the actor on row ten, and clear flag bit 6.
Clear bit 6 in the slot flags and preserve the rest.
Set dimensions ten by nineteen and state twelve, with $E9F0/$EA80 both two, $E780 at eight and $EB10 at $80.
Write state $0C to $E930,X and return.
Set dimensions eleven by nineteen and state four. Set $E9F0/$EA80 to one, $E780 to sixteen and $E840 to twenty.
Set dimensions eleven by nineteen and set $E9F0/$EA80 to two. Continue through $C55A to enter state fourteen.
Set state $0E in $E930,X.
Set dimensions ten by eighteen, set $E9F0/$EA80 to two and four, select state two and set bit 7 of $EB10.
Set dimensions ten by nineteen with $E9F0/$EA80 at two and four, then enter the state-fourteen path at $C55A.
Set a disabled timer at $EA50 and dimensions eight by eleven. Set the extent fields to four and six, clear flag bit 6 and set bit 4.
Set dimensions two by three and $EA50,X to $FF. If the low three flag bits are nonzero, move them into the timer at $E840,X and clear those bits.
Set $E870 to fifteen and set flag bit 5, then enter the common path at $C5FB.
Set the timer value to thirty, then join the flag setup at $C5F3.
Set the timer value to fifteen before the shared flag setup.
Store the supplied timer in $E870 and set flag mask $34 before the common fragment initializer.
Store the flag byte, set bit zero of $EB10, disable the $EA50 timer and set both size fields to one.
Set flag bit 5 on the slot at X.

Set the parent's width and height fields to $24 and $3F, clear its counters and the shared sequence flags $1D/$1F, then allocate types $40–$45 at its position. Each linked slot stores the parent slot at $E900.
Zero the horizontal orbit phase, set the vertical phase to $40 and continue through the state initializer at $C69A.
Select state fourteen, set $EA50 to $FF and set flag bit 4.
Return immediately from the actor callback. The corresponding descriptor slot passes control through $15EB and this RTS returns to the engine.
When $1D is nonzero, record its low seven bits at $70 and set $1E to three. Replace the old actor with a type $2B at its position and store the new slot in $15.

Run $38BD, then select state four or two according to the test at $23B7. A carry from $2757 starts a twenty-count sequence. The other path handles motion and periodically spawns three type $3C actors using records at $C99E.
Copy the parent's coordinates with a three-unit horizontal offset and enter the linked-child updater at $CCF4.
Copy the parent's position with a vertical offset of $0280, then enter the linked-child updater at $CCF4.
Copy the parent slot's coordinates with a three-unit horizontal and $0280 vertical offset, then enter the shared frame and state copy.
Copy the parent's frame and state. Remove the linked actor when $390C is set or its parent changes type or is removed.
Jump to the RTS at $C7C7. The parent flag test has its own entry at $C7BB.
Mark the child for removal when its parent's flags at $E810,Y are zero or have bit zero set.
Choose frame $AB or $AC from flag bit 3 and enter the update shared at $C845.
Every eighth update, toggle the low bit of the two-bit frame offset and select its second bit from flag bit 3. Then enter the shared update at $C845.
Every second update, increment the four-frame phase. Select the frame-table group from the signed motion fields and the direction flag before entering the shared update at $C845.

Set $E780 to $10, call $275A and follow its carry along with the local timer and player checks. On a passing check, a zero seven-bit random value queues effect $3D. Then continue through $1B64 with $08 set to four.
The four groups of four frame offsets indexed at $C83F. On a nonzero $E7B0 the sign chooses group 0 or 4, and with $E780 nonzero the direction flag chooses group 8 or 12 when $E7B0 is zero.
Choose frame offset zero or two from actor flag bit 3. Update through $2742 and $275A. With carry clear, process the $E840 timer and use $1B75 with mode four when it reaches zero.
Call the test at $279E with A set to two, and on carry set run $2760 with A set to five.
On carry from the trigger test, select the three fragment records at $C962 and start spawning type $32 through $C900.
On carry from the trigger test, use the four records at $C971 to spawn type $32.
On carry from the trigger test, use the four entries at $C985. The path at $C900 spawns the selected actors and marks the original slot for removal.
Call the fragment spawner at $C907, then set the parent's removal flag through $2739.

Save A as the type and Y as the record count. Allocate one slot per five-byte record. Add the first two signed byte offsets to the parent's coarse coordinates and store the three remaining bytes in the child timer and motion fields.
The spawner writes the child type here before calling the allocator for each record.
Three five-byte child records. The fields are horizontal and vertical byte offsets, a timer copied to $E840 and $E870, then motion bytes for $E780 and $E7B0.
Four five-byte spawn records for the trigger at $C8DB, using the same tuple as $C962.
Five-byte tuples used by the trigger at $C8EF. That call takes four records and starts at this address.
A five-byte tuple between the end of the four-record group consumed at $C8EF and the start of the type $27 group. Its caller is open.
Three five-byte records selected by $C720 for the type $3C allocation.
Call the shared updater at $287A only while the stage glyph phase at $CBF7 equals zero.
On the first update without flag bit 2, toggle direction and set bit 2. After the tests at $2757 and $1A57 pass, spawn type $39 three rows below and set its timer to twenty.
Call $275A and update motion with $08 set to two. Every fifth tick, advance the low two frame bits and use flag bit 3 to choose the group indexed at $CA1E.
Two four-frame rows. The first is $A2/$A1/$A2/$A3 and the second is $A5/$A4/$A5/$A6. The direction flag selects the row.

Run the shared update and decrement $E840. On underflow, reload twenty and toggle direction, then use $2760 to decide whether to spawn the actor burst at $CA68. Independently toggle the frame every fifth tick.
Spawn four type $3B actors. Set motion bytes $C0 and $40 in $E7B0 on the first two, set $E780 to $40 in the other two, and toggle the final child's direction flag.
Allocate type $3B, set its $E870 timer to ten, and copy the parent's four coordinate bytes into its slot.

If $1F is set, increment actor state and set flag bit 6. Test the active player or both players in a two-player game, using $1D to gate the overlap test. On success call $216F and mark the actor for removal.

A carry from $22E5 advances the actor a row and updates the map. The $E840 timer either ends the actor or changes it to type $1A plus the timer, after which the routine updates its flags and checks for player contact.
Call the shared update and count down $E840. On underflow, spawn the four-actor burst and mark this slot for removal.
Count down the timer at $E870. Underflow removes the slot. Otherwise toggle bit 2 of $EB10 and run the shared update.
Run the shared update. Remove the slot when flag bit 2 is clear or when $E870 underflows. Otherwise preserve bit 2.
Return immediately from the LEVELJ actor callback. The stage glyph updater has a separate entry at $CB67.

Decrement the timer at $CBF6. When it underflows, reload $0A and advance the phase at $CBF7 modulo four. Copy 32 bytes backwards into $78D8–$78F7, replacing glyphs $1B–$1E in the playfield character set.
The four phase offsets $1F, $3F, $5F and $3F point to the last byte of each 32-byte animation frame relative to $CB96. The copying loop counts down from the selected end.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 0. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $1B–$1E.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 1 and 3. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $1B–$1E.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 2. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $1B–$1E.
Countdown in calls to the stage update. Underflow reloads it with $0A and advances the animation phase.
The update increments this value modulo four and uses it to index the backwards-copy offsets at $CB92.

Link the current slot to the orbiting actor at the index saved in $CD98. Choose state fourteen or one from the shared player test, start a twenty-count sequence when $275A returns carry, and otherwise flip flag bit 3 when the local $7F countdown expires.
Place the actor three coarse horizontal units from its parent and run the common update at $CCF4.
Copy the parent position and add $0280 vertically before the common update.
Copy the parent position with offsets of three coarse horizontal units and $0280 vertically.
Copy the parent's position and add five to its coarse vertical coordinate, including the incoming carry, then run the common update.
Copy the parent position, add three to its horizontal coarse coordinate, then add five plus the resulting carry to its vertical coarse coordinate.
Update the child and copy its parent's state. Mark the child for removal if $390C is set, the parent has changed from type $3F, or its flags show it has been removed.
A jump to the RTS at $CD29 between the removal path and the branch target at $CD1D.
The child survives this test while its parent's flag byte is nonzero with bit zero clear.

Save the slot at $CD98 and calculate two offsets from the table at $5300. For each axis, scale the sample by eight and add it to the parent's coordinate. The horizontal result also subtracts four coarse units. Advance each phase by four and continue through the common linked-child update.
The type $45 callback writes its slot here at $CD32. The type $3F update at $CBF8 uses that index to store the parent number.
